Forgiveness, adoption and new life are not commodities Christ hands over; they are what you have when you have him, and a gospel that offers the parcels without the Person breeds both legalism and antinomianism.

witness.quote: we become insensitive to the difference between offering the benefits of Christ

evidence: shipped text was a paraphrase (and listed 'sanctification' where the source lists 'justification, reconciliation, redemption, adoption'); corrected to the three verbatim sentences, ch. 2 'Grace in the Gospel' not ch. 3 (archive.org FTS hits wholechristlegal0000ferg)

fields.text: The benefits of the gospel are in Christ. They do not exist apart from him. They are ours only in him.
fields.insight: Ferguson against the legalism / antinomianism polarity: both errors detach the benefits from the Benefactor. Justification, reconciliation, redemption and adoption are not things Christ gives at a distance; they are ours only by being his.

entry.text: Holiness is Christlikeness. As the Spirit of Christ, the Holy Spirit is the agent of this transformation.
entry.insight: Ferguson's shortest definition of sanctification. Holiness has a face, and the Spirit's work is not to make us spiritual in general but to make us like the Son; Romans 8:29 is the job description.

entry.text: Union with Christ is the foundation of all our spiritual experience and all spiritual blessings.
entry.insight: Ferguson's structural claim, and the reason he gives union with Christ its own chapter before the benefits. Every blessing is downstream of being in him; treat the blessings as detachable and the Christian life turns into a checklist.

entry.ref: The Holy Spirit (1996), on sanctification
entry.text: In a word, for the New Testament, sanctification, or holiness, is Christlikeness or, as various theologians throughout the history of the church have described it, 'Christiformity'.
entry.insight: Ferguson borrowing an old word to say a plain thing: holiness is being formed into the shape of Christ. That relocates sanctification from a list of rules to a Person, and it means the more you know him the more you will resemble him.

witness.quote: sanctification, or holiness, is Christlikeness

entry.ref: The Drama of Doctrine (2005), 'Faith Seeking Understanding: Sources and Norms'
entry.text: Doctrine has to do with what faith seeking understanding gets when its search is successful. To be precise: Christian doctrine is the reward that faith finds at the end of its search for the meaning of the apostolic testimony to what God was doing in the event of Jesus Christ.
entry.insight: Vanhoozer's definition of doctrine, keeping Anselm's formula intact. Doctrine is not a set of abstractions layered over the gospel but the understanding faith reaches when it takes the apostles' witness to Christ seriously enough to ask what it means.

witness.quote: Doctrine has to do with what faith seeking understanding gets when its search is successful

entry.ref: Is There a Meaning in This Text? (1998), ch. 5
entry.text: I now wish to define the text as a communicative act of a communicative agent fixed by writing.
entry.insight: Vanhoozer's answer to the death of the author. A text is someone doing something with words, and reading well means recovering what the author did; the reader owes the author that much, and owes God that much when the text is Scripture.

entry.text: Doctrine proceeds from an authoritative script and gives direction as to how individuals and the church can participate fittingly in the drama of redemption.
entry.insight: Vanhoozer's thesis sentence. Scripture is the script, doctrine is the stage direction, and the church is the company that has to perform; doctrine that is never enacted has stopped one step short of its purpose.

entry.ref: Biblical Authority after Babel (2016), conclusion
entry.text: Mere Protestant Christianity uses the resources of the solas and the priesthood of all believers to express the unity-in-diversity that local churches have in Christ.
entry.insight: Vanhoozer's defence of Protestantism against the charge that sola scriptura only breeds division. The five solas and the priesthood of believers are the resources for a unity that does not require uniformity, which is what the New Testament churches already had.

entry.text: This book, then, aims for something deeper than a new technique or a call to action: to consider Christ, that he might become more central for you, that you might know him better, treasure him more and enter into his joy.

entry.ref: Gentle and Lowly (2020), ch. 2
entry.text: Time and again it is the morally disgusting, the socially reviled, the inexcusable and undeserving, who do not simply receive Christ's mercy but to whom Christ most naturally gravitates.
entry.insight: Ortlund reading the Gospels for where Jesus actually goes. His mercy is not a reluctant concession to the worst people; they are the ones he moves toward, which is bad news for the respectable and very good news for everyone who knows what they are.
